A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure shorten the time from first symptom to treatment start for lung cancer patients, and by how many days?
Measure: Standardised lung cancer pathway with booked slots. A lung cancer pathway on the Danish/Swedish/Norwegian model: fixed referral criteria, pre-booked CT, PET-CT, bronchoscopy and MDT slots, a named pathway owner, and published time limits for each step.
supported_en: In Sweden the lung cancer pathway's lead time is 30–44 days, and only 30 % of patients started treatment within it (Scientific Reports 2023).
not_supported_en: No page we read measures days saved by a lung cancer pathway, so the assumed saving of 14 days (range 5–23) is not shown.

in_use_source.title: Uusi ohje terveydenhuollon ammattilaisille keuhkosyövän diagnostiikasta julkaistu

summary_en: HUS publishes a lung cancer pathway description for patients. It covers a referral to the lung clinic, booked appointments sent by letter, and a multidisciplinary team that reviews cases "when needed". The page shows no fixed time limits for each step, no pre-booked CT, PET-CT or bronchoscopy slots, and no named pathway owner. In May 2026, Filha reported that the National Lung Cancer Programme's working group had published a diagnostic guideline that introduces a standard referral to specialist care, a single pathway and target times for starting treatment. For the effect, the Swedish study we already held (Scientific Reports 2023) gives a lung cancer lead time of 30–44 days, met by only 30 % of patients, but it does not report how many days the pathway saved.
unanswered_en: I found no page showing whether HUS or Keusote has adopted the national target times, or whether imaging and bronchoscopy slots are pre-booked.
